## Trial `password-complexity-policy-cento__pccSMqP`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The task's password complexity requirements (minlen=12, minclass=3) were correctly implemented via a pwquality.conf.d drop-in on node1, with PAM wiring confirmed and enforcement functionally demonstrated through pwscore both before and after a genuine, well-evidenced reboot (distinct boot_ids, connection drop, recovered state). ### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long
  - **Why:** A pwquality drop-in (/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/10-complexity.conf) was created with minlen=12, and pam_pwquality.so is wired into both /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth (pre-existing PAM stack, confirmed present). Functional verification via pwscore showed an 11-character password rejected with the explicit message 'shorter than 12 characters', and this behavior persisted after a full reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b7d4d06a1f9447a6`, `cmd-d5c99ff4dc2242b7`, `cmd-ae353c21095a47cf`, `cmd-725727ad45fc460b`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes
  - **Why:** minclass=3 was set in the same drop-in file. Functional verification confirmed a 15-char lowercase-only password and a 12-char two-class password were both rejected for 'less than 3 character classes' (the second failed on a dictionary check first but the minclass mechanism was independently demonstrated by the lowercase-only case), while a 12-char three-class random password (score 36) was accepted. Re-verified identically after reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b7d4d06a1f9447a6`, `cmd-a0911c8c3a2f4ccf`, `cmd-a1f75b29efbf458e`, `cmd-725727ad45fc460b`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Configuration persists and enforcement is durable across a restart of node1
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id (d052eb57...) was captured alongside the config/PAM state; a backgrounded systemctl reboot returned an acknowledgement before the connection dropped; the connection then failed twice (timeout, reset) consistent with an actual reboot; a new boot_id (7a149124...) was observed afterward, matching the global after_executor snapshot; and the drop-in file, PAM wiring, and pwscore enforcement behavior (reject <12 chars, accept 3-class 12-char) were all re-confirmed post-reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0ec998a595e04182`, `cmd-75433305dfc84250`, `cmd-c9910acbcb414385`, `cmd-e9ccfdc965fa46b6`, `cmd-55ff181aeb8f4c30`, `cmd-1995280cbe5146cf`, `cmd-725727ad45fc460b`

### Comments and limitations

- Enforcement was verified via pwscore against the pwquality library directly rather than by attempting an actual `passwd` change for a real user through the PAM stack, though this is a standard and reasonable verification method given the same PAM module and config are used.
- The 12-char two-class test case (cmd-a0911c8c3a2f4ccf) was rejected by a dictionary check rather than directly by the minclass rule, so minclass enforcement for that specific case is inferred rather than directly isolated; the lowercase-only case in the same command more directly confirms minclass=3 behavior.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.950); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
